lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3, what three jobs does your skeleton do? (It supports you, protects soft parts and lets you move.) Today: the bones, joints and muscles that move you, and how they work together.

An adult's skeleton has 206 bones. It does four jobs: support (it holds you up and gives you shape), protection and movement (muscles pull on bones). And it makes blood cells, in the soft marrow inside big bones.

Protection: your skull guards your brain, and your ribs guard your heart and lungs. The bones of your spine (backbone) guard the spinal cord: the bundle of nerves that carries messages to and from your brain.

Bones are alive: they grow, and they mend when they break. Calcium makes them hard: milk, yoghurt and green leaves give you calcium, sunlight helps your skin make vitamin D, and exercise makes bones stronger.

A joint is where bones meet. Ligaments hold them together and smooth cartilage cushions their ends. Elbows and knees are hinge joints (one way); shoulders and hips are ball and socket joints (every way).

A muscle can only pull: it contracts (gets shorter and fatter) and pulls a bone by a tendon, a tough cord. So muscles work in pairs: to bend your arm, the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes; to straighten it, the triceps contracts.

Your legs have pairs too: the hamstrings at the back of the thigh bend your knee, and the quadriceps at the front straighten it. A pivot joint at the top of your neck turns your head; skull joints are fixed.

Try it in the world: rest one hand on your upper arm and slowly bend and straighten your elbow. Feel the biceps bulge as it contracts, then the triceps at the back. Next: nutrition and digestion, the food your bones and muscles need.

exercises.prompt: How many bones are in an adult's skeleton?
exercises.explain: An adult has 206 bones; a baby has more, and some join together as it grows.

exercises.hint: Which bone is round your head?
exercises.explain: The skull is a hard case round the brain.

exercises.prompt: Muscles can push as well as pull.
exercises.hint: What does a muscle do when it contracts?
exercises.explain: False: muscles only pull, so they work in pairs to move a bone both ways.

exercises.prompt: The arm is bending. Which muscle is contracting?
exercises.hint: The contracting muscle is short and fat, pulling the forearm up.
exercises.explain: The biceps, on the front of the upper arm, contracts; the triceps relaxes.

exercises.prompt: Match each job of the skeleton to what it means.
exercises.hint: Say what each job means for your body.
exercises.explain: Support: holds you up. Protection: guards your organs. Movement: muscles pull on bones. Blood cells: made in the marrow.

exercises.prompt: Your ribs come in 12 pairs. How many ribs is that?
Label the skeleton: tap a word, then its number.
exercises.hint: The skull is at the top, the ribs round the chest; the humerus is in the upper arm and the femur in the thigh.
exercises.explain: Skull: the head. Ribs: round the chest. Humerus: the upper arm. Pelvis: the hips. Femur: the thigh.

exercises.prompt: Label the arm: tap a word, then its number.
exercises.hint: The biceps is on top, the triceps underneath; the tendon joins muscle to bone; the joint is where bones meet.
exercises.explain: Biceps: the top muscle (contracting here). Triceps: underneath. Tendon: the cord from the biceps to the forearm. Elbow joint: where the bones meet.

exercises.prompt: This joint is in your shoulder. What kind of joint is it?
exercises.hint: A round end sits in a cup. How many ways can it turn?
exercises.explain: A ball and socket joint, like the shoulder and hip, turns every way.

exercises.prompt: Sort the joints: hinge, or ball and socket?
exercises.hint: Hinges move one way, like a door; ball and socket joints turn every way.
exercises.explain: Hinge: elbow, knee, finger joints. Ball and socket: shoulder, hip.

exercises.prompt: Ligaments join bone to bone at a joint.
exercises.hint: Tendons join muscle to bone. What holds two bones together?
exercises.explain: True: ligaments are tough bands between bones; tendons join muscles to bones.

exercises.prompt: To straighten your leg, which muscle contracts?
exercises.hint: The muscle at the front of the thigh pulls the lower leg forward.
exercises.explain: The quadriceps contracts to straighten the knee, and the hamstrings relax.

exercises.prompt: Why are muscles found in pairs?
choices: each can only pull, one way each
one is spare in case one breaks
exercises.hint: Think about what a muscle can and cannot do.
exercises.explain: A muscle can only pull. One pulls a bone one way and its partner pulls it back.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps in order to lift a cup to your mouth.
items: Nerves carry it to the biceps
The tendon pulls the forearm up
The cup rises to your mouth
exercises.hint: Start with the brain and end with the cup.
exercises.explain: The brain sends a message along nerves; the biceps contracts; its tendon pulls the forearm; the cup rises.

exercises.prompt: A new baby has around 300 bones and an adult 206. Why?
choices: some bones join together as we grow
exercises.hint: Think about the soft parts of a baby's skull.
exercises.explain: Some of a baby's bones, such as the plates of the skull, join together as it grows, so an adult has fewer.

exercises.prompt: Red blood cells are made in the marrow inside some bones.
exercises.hint: What does the soft inside of a big bone do?
exercises.explain: True: bone marrow makes red and white blood cells.

exercises.prompt: Label the arm as it straightens: tap a word, then its number.
exercises.hint: The fat muscle underneath is contracting; the bone runs from the shoulder to the elbow.
exercises.explain: Biceps on top (relaxing), triceps underneath (contracting), the tendon to the forearm, the humerus in the upper arm, and the elbow joint where the bones meet.

exercises.prompt: Which helps keep your bones strong?
exercises.hint: What do bones need to be hard, and what makes them stronger?
exercises.explain: Calcium makes bones hard, vitamin D (made in sunlight) helps you take it in, and exercise makes bones stronger.
